source: Kevin Maroufkhani · Recorded debrief with original TTI report visuals

chapters.title: DISC · Welcome, Kevin
chapters.text: Hi Kevin. I'm so happy to have this opportunity to debrief you on your assessment results. We're going to start by looking at your DISC, which means it depicts how you do what you do. It dives into your behavioral profile. And if you notice there are two different graphs in here. Graph One is Adapted, and Graph Two is Natural. Natural style is how you choose to behave at home. And adapted is how you modify your behavior in the workplace or outside the house. If you notice there's zero to a hundred and in the middle there's a gray bar at 50. What this means is anything above the line, a 50 line, we say that's a high behavior. Anything below the line, we say that's a low behavior. What you have the most of is called core behavior. And if you notice at home, your core behavior is dominance, red, and at work it becomes your yellow, which is influencing. So let's talk about what all this means.

chapters.title: DISC · Dominance
chapters.text: Well, D stands for dominance and that stands for how we solve problems and challenges. Yellow stands for influencing and that deals with people and contacts. The S stands for steadiness and that stands for pace and consistency. And C stands for conscientiousness or compliance and deals with rules and regulations and detailed analysis. If you notice your D is very, very high. So what does that mean? With your high dominance, you become very assertive, competitive, confident, bottom line focused, and you take charge. And you would be having some issues with people that are lower dominant people because they tend to be more agreeable, collaborative, low key, accommodating, and consensus seeking. You are someone who takes charge and just moves forward. So one thing you want to tell people around you, especially at home, is when people are trying to communicate with you, it's best for them to be brief and direct, focus on results and bottom line, and don't tell you what to do, but offer you solutions. And you also like people to be confident and kind of business-like. The way you don't like to be communicated to is if people ramble on or explain to you, if they get overly personal or emotional, if they waste time on small talk, or be vague. It's interesting because your high dominance also stands for being urgent, quick, and people with high dominance like yours usually tend to be very much into trying to solve problems after problems after problems. So the more things you could solve, the happier you are. The emotion behind it is frustration or anger. So when this might happen is when you're around people who do not share your urgency, who do not share your sense of pace. That's a very high pace.

chapters.title: DISC · Influence
chapters.text: On the influencing side, you're at 78 on the natural and it goes up to 82 on the adapted side. So what that really means is that you are absolutely a social butterfly. You could be around people, you could communicate with people, you could be persuasive, you're sociable, expressive, energetic, and optimistic. You could also be very, very warm and enthusiastic. What that really means is that if you're confronted with a problem, the first thing you look at is whether or not I can solve this problem or not. So your high I says, yes, I'm going to do it. And D says, I'm sure I can do it. Because a high dominance says, I can conquer my environment. And in your particular case, when the D and I are so close to one another, that tells you that you could solve mostly people-related problems, and you have no problem with that. The high I also means you could be very artistic, could also be extremely communicative, and very good with people. And you have no problem meeting a stranger and striking a conversation and being able to get along with them just fine.

chapters.title: DISC · Steadiness
chapters.text: The next one, as you notice, it says S. Now, S stands for steadiness and deals with pace and consistency. As your S goes higher, you become slower, but become far more consistent and reliable. As your S goes down, you become multitasking, you become more of someone who is just almost like restless, but it's almost like active. So much activity where sometimes you drive yourself to being very exhausted. Now, the emotional side of this is non-expression. But since you're 36 and 42, that means for the most part, what you see is what you get, and you're able to express how you're feeling, and people can see what you're doing. People with high S are usually calm, loyal, supportive, good listeners, and consistent. People with low S, which would be you, tend to be restless, spontaneous, adaptable, multitasking, and impatient. When people have a high S, the way you communicate with them is we become patient and sincere. We need to explain changes very quickly, easily, early, and step-by-step. We also need to show how it affects people. We need to ask for their opinion directly. People with low S, they enjoy keeping up the good pace. They enjoy, they don't like rigid routines. They like multitasking. They like different things. Don't over-explain process to a low S and bog them down with too much procedures. And if you notice, you raise it from 36 to 42, which means at work you become a little bit more procedural.

chapters.title: DISC · Compliance
chapters.text: The next one on the list, but not least, is your low compliance. People with low compliance tend to be flexible, independent, casual, big picture, and risk-tolerant. The emotion behind C is fear or cautiousness. Obviously, it's opposite of the high dominant. And when you have a high D and a low C, that makes you someone who is very bold, daring, risk-taking, and you do things that most people at the beginning will say, well, questions, say, are you sure you want to do this? And you say, yes, I'm sure. I'm confident in my own ability. I can solve any problem. I can communicate to people. Yes, I can get it done. Now, when you're dealing with people that are high C, high C stands for being analytical, precise, systematic, detail-oriented, and quality-focused. And they're extremely focused on doing things right. In your case, you do it and you say, okay, let's see what happens next. So, Kevin, a couple of things that are really important to notice here.

chapters.title: DISC · Natural and Adapted styles
chapters.text: First of all, you have adaptation on your profile. You go from a conducting persuader to a persuading promoter, which means at home, you're able to act almost like a James Bond character. You can mix action with charm. You can be charming, communicative, salesy, or you can be very direct to the point and get things done. Both red and yellow, which is dominance and influencing, are fast behaviors. At work, maybe because of the nature of the work you do, you adapt quite a bit to becoming a persuading promoter. What this means is you're able to sell an ice cube to an Eskimo. You're able to relate to all types of humanity. So you have a very powerful brain when it comes to being able to deal with people, understand people, and also sell to them.

chapters.title: DISC · Adaptation and inherited patterns
chapters.text: A couple of things going back to your DISC profile. Because of the changes from 92 dominance to 66 dominance, from 78 to 82 influencing, from 36 S to 42 steady, and from 8 to 12 on compliance, what this shows is that there's a bit of generational epigenetic patterns that I see in you. What this means is somehow you've adapted and adopted patterns that have been passed down to you from five generations. That means you could have 32 different variables that you have drawn from. So this could be something, for example, your great-great-grandfather did. Maybe your dad did. Maybe your great-grandmother did. So these are the behavioral changes that have been passed down to you, and you've adopted them as your own. When you took this assessment, because your dominance was being impacted so severely, you may have been under some kind of a stress, and you were having to become more submissive than you choose to be. If you notice, your blue even goes from 8 to 12, which is an increase of four points. So I would say your adaptive profile style perhaps was working for you, but because of all these changes, there's a really good possibility that you were under some stress, and if you continue that pattern, you may have stayed under that stress pattern. Kevin, next we'll go into your motivational intelligence and your acumen.

chapters.title: Driving Forces · Return on investment
chapters.text: Kevin, it's good to talk to you again. We're going to dive right into what's called driving forces. Each one of us is motivated in a certain way. Kevin, on your driving force graph, you'll see that there are six categories in the center, knowledge, utility, surrounding, others, power, and methods. And if you notice on each side, you will see the opposites. For example, knowledge is intellectual and instinctive. Kevin, you also notice there's a small number and there's a big number. The big number shows the intensity score for that driver, and the little number ranks it from one to 12. So we're going to jump right into utility, which is your number one driver. Utility talks about return on investment of time, money, and energy. Your Selfless score is 8. And because your Resourceful score is 89, what that tells me is that you are extremely focused on full and maximum return on investment. And remember, because of your high D and low C, sometimes you take chances that most people would find very careless almost, but you make them happen. So the need to attract more return is always pushing you to take more and more chances. I would say your resourcefulness also could be very powerful in you wanting to help people solve people-related issues, such as marketing, such as sales, such as if I do this, this will come back to me like X plus Y.

chapters.title: Driving Forces · Innovation and instinct
chapters.text: When it's combined with your number two, which is receptiveness, if you notice your structure is only 26, which means you're not very traditional. You don't like structured way of living. Your number two motivator is receptive. So what that really means is that you are really keen on innovation and change. And you're very open to new things. Kevin, when we look at your number three, which is called instinctive, and the opposite is Intellectual at 24 versus Instinctive at 53. You're saying, as long as I know it works, I'm going to rely on my past experiences, and also I want to rely on my gut. And so when it comes to decision making, you're very instinctive.

chapters.title: Driving Forces · Helping others
chapters.text: When we look at your number four, if you notice with others, you see intentional and altruistic. Now this is very interesting because you're somewhat altruistic at 33, but more Intentional at 46. So this would be, I'm sure you've heard the expression, if you want to feed someone, teach them how to fish and they eat for a lifetime. You will help people at one point. You're just going to say, listen, enough is enough. You got to do this on your own. You got to become more independent. Don't depend on me so much to do things for you, especially if you find out that you're losing your precious resources, such as, again, time, money, and energy.

chapters.title: Driving Forces · Power and surroundings
chapters.text: When it comes to taking power or giving power, you're almost like dead in the center, but some things you take full ownership, full command and get in front of it and make it happen. But in many cases, you also like to collaborate with people. You also like to enjoy building consensus, asking people, what do you think? How do you think we should do this? The same way is true for your surroundings, which means when it comes to, I'm motivated by how things feel or I'm motivated by how things function. You kind of choose both. You like the objectivity. At the same time, you like beauty. You like things to make sense. You like people to get along. And so you have a pretty balanced motivational drivers, except for resourcefulness and receptive, which are really the key, key motivators for you.

chapters.title: Acumen · World View
chapters.text: So I'm going to jump right in to your acumen, which I found to be very interesting because if you notice on your graph, you have worldview and you have self-view. When it comes to working and seeing the world outside of yourself, we look at people, we look at tasks or practical thinking, we look at systems. All three are extremely high. And for example, understanding people, you're at 96% and you're way above the norm, which means you use your ability to understand people. You also use your ability to get along with people and to know people, to bring you your return on investment. If you notice there's an up and down arrow, which means you don't overvalue or undervalue people. You just see them for what they are. You're extremely able and clear how to perform the duties and tasks you need to perform. And again, if you can see up and down arrow, which means to you, you do what you have to do. When it comes to looking at systems, big picture, pixels in it, small pixels put in together, make it a big picture, you have a very high systems judgment. What that means is that you're able to easily take a look at something like a strategy and you can take it from point A to point Z very easily.

chapters.title: Acumen · Self View and inherited patterns
chapters.text: On the other side, you see it says self view. If you notice, Kevin, it says sense of self at 60 percent, which means you're kind of struggling a little bit. You're kind of self-aware, but you're trying to really, and the down arrow is down, which means I want to learn. I want to better myself. I am successful. I've done many good things in the outside world, but inside of me, I'm still a bit unaware. So there's a bit of a low sense of confidence also, to be honest, internally, and I think at this point, you could easily move that up by understanding your full potential, which is amazing. And this is probably predicated upon some earlier self-perception. And if you remember, I told you you also had some epigenetic background that had been passed down to you. So to me, because your worldview is so powerful, some of this could be an overlay of parents, grandparents, great-grandparents, something like that that's been overlaid on you. And if you can separate yourself from what you've inherited and move on with your life, I think you will see a huge, huge, huge change. When you took this assessment though, your role awareness was okay, was good, but there was a slight down arrow which meant, if you notice, I said it appeared to me at the time you were under some stress. And so you were not really liking a couple of the roles you're playing in life.

chapters.title: Acumen · Future, purpose and vision
chapters.text: When it comes to your future, if you notice there's an up and down arrow with good clarity, what you're asking yourself is, okay, I've done really well, I'm happy with life, and I know future is going to be okay, but what is it that I really want? Number one is, what's my purpose in life? Another one is, what's my passion in life? And more importantly, what's my vision in life? Where do I want to be? How do I want to get there? And how happy am I going to be when I'm not only there, but on my journey? You're so accomplishment focused that sometimes you forget to stop and smell the roses, to really enjoy the moment. So my recommendation is to take a look at where you're at in life and breathe. Take a deep breath and say, wow, I'm doing great. I have a very good life. I've accomplished so much. I want to enjoy it at least for a few minutes.

chapters.title: Acumen · Perspective and confidence
chapters.text: You're a bit idealistic when it comes to outside situations, which means sometimes you wish things were different. So sometimes maybe you want to take a look at, I want to look at what is real, what is idealistic, what is realistic. When it comes to your own self, you have a very high emotional bias distortion of 32 points, which means you tend to be very hard on yourself. But there's always this nagging, the whispering in your ear, the Kevin, you need to be more. You need to be more. You're not good enough. You're not good enough. The truth is you're plenty good enough. And if I were you, I would take a look at releasing these negative voices that come into your mind and just acknowledge your greatness as you are.

chapters.title: Acumen · Strengths and outlook
chapters.text: You have tremendous ability for external problem-solving decision making. And so use those to your benefit. Your attitude index is open-minded, accessible, flexible, appreciative, grateful, thankful, approving, favorable, dynamic, lively, energetic, vibrant, positive, encouraging, upbeat. Use these words that I just mentioned to raise your self-confidence, to raise your sense of self.
